newsitem.title: USA: Africa, East Europe critical food areas - Borlaug.
newsitem.headline: Africa, East Europe critical food areas - Borlaug.

text.p: Sub-Saharan Africa and former Soviet nations in Eastern Europe will be the critical areas for food production for the next decade, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Norman Borlaug said on Thursday.

Borlaug said in an interview that in Africa agricultural progress needed to be teamed with economic development, while food problems in Eastern Europe caused by political upheaval had the benefit of an advanced shipping and educational system.
"The two critical areas for the next decade, I'd say, are the African countries south of the Sahara and the (Eastern European) ex-Soviet Union," he said.

Borlaug was awarded the Peace Prize in 1970 for his work as a wheat breeder in the so-called Green Revolution of high-yielding wheat and rice varieties that foiled forecasts of famine in Asia by the 1970s.

Now 83, he is an adviser to International Maize (corn) and Wheat Improvement Centre, where he won the Peace Prize, a university professor and president of a foundation assisting in agricultural development in Africa.

Africa has long been fraught by food underproduction. The U.S. Agriculture Department estimates sub-Saharan Africa's food aid needs at 3.4 million metric tons this year despite a bumper grain crop. The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation estimated last November that 22 million people in the region faced "food emergencies of varying intensity."

In many African nations, Borlaug said, the population was predominantly rural, with farmers tilling small plots. Experimental plots show yields can "double, triple or quadruple" with use of improved varieties, proper planting dates, weed control and fertilisers, he said.
